description: Indian and world classics — author identification

questions.stem: The autobiography 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' was written by:
questions.explanation: Gandhi began writing his autobiography in 1925 (serialised in Navjivan in Gujarati). It covers his life up to 1921. Nehru wrote 'An Autobiography' / 'Toward Freedom' and 'The Discovery of India'. Tilak wrote 'Gita Rahasya' (from jail in Mandalay). Bose wrote 'The Indian Struggle'. Abul Kalam Azad's 'India Wins Freedom' is another key political autobiography of the period.

questions.stem: 'A Brief History of Time', a famous popular-science book on cosmology, was written by:
questions.explanation: Hawking's 1988 bestseller introduced general readers to black holes, the Big Bang and the arrow of time. Feynman wrote 'Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!' and 'The Feynman Lectures on Physics'. Sagan wrote 'Cosmos' and 'Pale Blue Dot'. Brian Greene wrote 'The Elegant Universe' on string theory. Hawking later wrote 'The Universe in a Nutshell' and 'Brief Answers to the Big Questions'.

questions.stem: Match the book with its author. A. 'Midnight's Children'. B. 'The God of Small Things'. C. 'Malgudi Days'. D. 'The White Tiger'. List-II: 1. Salman Rushdie, 2. Arundhati Roy, 3. R. K. Narayan, 4. Aravind Adiga.
questions.explanation: Midnight's Children — Salman Rushdie (Booker 1981, Booker of Bookers 1993 and 2008). The God of Small Things — Arundhati Roy (Booker 1997). Malgudi Days — R. K. Narayan (short-story cycle set in the fictional town of Malgudi). The White Tiger — Aravind Adiga (Booker 2008). Kiran Desai ('The Inheritance of Loss', 2006) is India's fourth Booker winner.

questions.stem: The novel 'War and Peace' was written by the Russian author:
questions.explanation: Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910) wrote War and Peace (1869) — set during the Napoleonic wars — and Anna Karenina (1877). Dostoevsky wrote Crime and Punishment, The Brothers Karamazov, The Idiot. Chekhov wrote the plays The Cherry Orchard and Uncle Vanya plus short stories. Gorky wrote the novel Mother and plays like The Lower Depths.

questions.stem: 'Wings of Fire', an autobiography that became a bestseller in India, was written by:
questions.explanation: Kalam co-wrote 'Wings of Fire' (1999) with Arun Tiwari — covering his life up to the 1998 Pokhran II tests. Other Kalam books include 'India 2020', 'Ignited Minds' and 'Turning Points'. Vikram Sarabhai (father of the Indian space programme), Homi Bhabha (atomic energy pioneer) and C. V. Raman (1930 Nobel for the Raman effect) did not write autobiographies of comparable reach.

questions.stem: The classic Indian epic 'Ramayana', attributed to sage Valmiki, is written in:
questions.explanation: Valmiki's Ramayana — composed in Sanskrit — has about 24,000 verses in seven kandas (books). Tulsidas's 'Ramcharitmanas' (16th century) is the Awadhi version. Kamban's 'Iramavataram' is the Tamil version. Pali was the language of the Theravada Buddhist canon (Tripitaka). Prakrit was a family of Middle Indo-Aryan vernaculars; Ashokan edicts were mostly in Prakrit.

questions.stem: 'The Origin of Species' (1859), which proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, was written by:
questions.explanation: Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection' (1859) revolutionised biology. He later wrote 'The Descent of Man' (1871) on human evolution. Lamarck had proposed an earlier (and largely incorrect) theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics. Gregor Mendel worked out the laws of heredity separately through his pea-plant experiments (1866). T. H. Huxley was Darwin's leading public defender ('Darwin's bulldog').
